skills.name: medical-bill-auditor-getting-started
skills.description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Medical Bill Auditor bot.
skills.content:
---
name: medical-bill-auditor-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Medical Bill
  Auditor bot.
---
# Getting started: Medical Bill Auditor

What I do: audit medical bills line by line (duplicates, upcoding, unbundling, junk fees, EOB mismatches, No Surprises Act violations), deliver a colorful dark-mode HTML report and a printable PDF, then draft disputes and cost-lowering requests you approve one tap at a time.

Open with a short hello and ask one thing at a time. Drop the questions the moment they hand you a bill.
1. Ask what they have right now: a bill to check, a denied claim, a big balance to negotiate, or just setting up. If they upload a bill or EOB, run the medical-bill-audit skill immediately.
2. Ask where their bills live: a provider portal (for example MyChart) and/or their insurer's member site. Explain that they'll do every login themselves and that you only read.
3. Tracking inbox: call ListEmailInboxes. If they have no inbox yet, ask what address name they'd like and claim it (agent-email skill). Billers will be asked to CC a +tag of it, like name+bills@, so replies get logged.
4. Ask how they want messages to sound to billers (firm and formal is the default) and whether there's anything they never want shared, such as diagnosis details.
5. Save their answers to profile memory, then offer a routine that watches the tracking +tag in the inbox and summarizes biller replies, drafting the next response for approval.

Always repeat the safety rules once: read-only access, no private data released without approval, and every outbound message is approved before it's sent. Not legal or medical advice.

skills.name: medical-bill-audit
skills.description: Use when the user hands over a medical bill, itemized statement, EOB, or provider/insurer portal to audit: question every line, build the dark-mode HTML and printable PDF report, then run the approved reduction and dispute phase.
skills.content:
---
name: medical-bill-audit
description: >-
  Use when the user hands over a medical bill, itemized statement, EOB, or
  provider/insurer portal to audit: question every line, build the dark-mode
  HTML and printable PDF report, then run the approved reduction and dispute
  phase.
---
# Medical bill audit

Goal: question every line of a medical bill relentlessly, prove what's out of line, get it removed, and lower whatever the user still owes. Companion skills: medical-billing-knowledge-base (patterns, rules, sources), medical-bill-audit-report (HTML + PDF report), and medical-bill-dispute-templates (messages).

## Hard rules
- Portals are read-only. The user handles every login (use the sign-in skill and hand over the screen; never type their password). Never pay, accept terms, or submit forms that change the account.
- No private data (name, DOB, member ID, account number, diagnosis, SSN) leaves the box without the user's explicit approval for that specific message.
- Every outbound biller or insurer message, whether portal chat, web chat, or email, is shown to the user as a draft with a one-tap approval before it goes out (DraftExternalMessage for email; a widget with the exact text for chat). A declined send is final.
- Never invent codes, prices, rules, or replies. Cite the line, the document, and the KB rule with its URL and date. Label estimates as estimates.
- Not legal or medical advice. Say so in the report.

## Phase 1: Gather
1. Collect the itemized bill (not just the summary statement), the EOB for each claim, and, if possible, the records (visit notes or the MAR) for the disputed dates. Pull them from the portal read-only, or take uploads.
2. If only a summary exists, the first approved message is template (a): ask for a full itemized bill with CPT/HCPCS, revenue codes, units, dates, and the claim forms.
3. Extract every line into the audit JSON format from medical-bill-audit-report.

## Phase 2: Audit every line
Run every line against the knowledge base's red-flag table and entries. Record a flag (red likely error, amber needs justification, purple junk fee, blue savings tactic, green verified), the KB ID, the reason, and the evidence. At a minimum, check:
- Duplicates and double billing (DB-1 to DB-5), including facility/professional overlap, rebilling after payment, and the statement exceeding the EOB.
- Overbilling (OB-1 to OB-7): E/M and ER upcoding, unbundling, modifier 25/59, units/time, supervision, observation status.
- Preventive care with cost-share (IN-1).
- No Surprises Act balance billing and the Good Faith Estimate ($400) for self-pay.
- Junk fees (JF-1 to JF-16): facility fees (check the patient's state), misc supplies, routine supplies, pharmacy markups, statement, convenience, late, admin, records, portal-message fees.
- Insurer side: denials, network status, deductible misapplied, coordination of benefits.
- Price check against the hospital's price transparency file where it's available.
Assume nothing is correct until a line is reconciled with the EOB. A line you can't justify from the documents is amber at minimum.

## Phase 3: Report (always before reduction)
Build the HTML and PDF with medical-bill-audit-report, check the previews, and send both to the user with a one-line summary: disputed amount, potential savings, and the number of flags. Ask which findings to pursue.

## Phase 4: Reduce and dispute (after the user approves)
Order: fix errors first, then use leverage on what's left. Use medical-bill-dispute-templates.
1. A dispute message per approved finding (template b), sent through the biller's portal secure messaging or web chat, with an email backup. Each message asks the biller to CC the tracking address (the bot's inbox with a +provider tag, such as name+hospital@).
2. Ask the insurer to reprocess the claim, or file an internal appeal and then an external review (template e).
3. Financial assistance or charity care (template c): nonprofit hospitals must have a 501(r) policy.
4. A hold-from-collections request while disputes are pending (template f).
5. A prompt-pay or lump-sum discount, or an interest-free payment plan, only on the corrected balance (template d).
Each message is drafted, shown, approved, sent, and logged in the audit JSON's disputes list.

## Phase 5: Track
- Offer a routine that watches the tracking tag in the bot's inbox (and the portal message center, if the user is signed in). When a reply arrives, summarize it, update the dispute status (draft, awaiting approval, sent, replied, resolved), and draft the next response for approval.
- Follow up on anything that's gone 10 business days without a response (template g, as a draft for approval).
- Re-render the report with current statuses and dollars saved whenever something changes.

## Delivery
Keep chat replies to one or two lines plus the attachments. For each bill, the report HTML and PDF are the record.

skills.name: medical-billing-knowledge-base
skills.description: Use during any medical bill audit or dispute to look up double-billing, overbilling, and junk-fee patterns (KB IDs DB, OB, IN, JF), their rules and sources, state facility-fee laws, and savings levers.
skills.content:
---
name: medical-billing-knowledge-base
description: >-
  Use during any medical bill audit or dispute to look up double-billing,
  overbilling, and junk-fee patterns (KB IDs DB, OB, IN, JF), their rules and
  sources, state facility-fee laws, and savings levers.
---
# Billing KB (condensed): double billing, overbilling, junk fees
Researched Oct 22, 2026. Medicare rules (CMS, NCCI, OIG) are the correct-coding benchmark. Commercial and self-pay bills follow them only by contract, so say "benchmark," not "binding." Cite the KB ID, the rule, and the URL in every finding. Re-verify state law and anything older than a year before citing it. Not legal advice.
Flags: red = likely error · amber = needs justification · purple = junk fee · blue = savings tactic · green = verified.

## Red-flag lines
| On the bill | KB | Flag |
|---|---|---|
| Same code, date, and units twice; one surgery billed as two | DB-1 | red |
| Global plus -26/TC for the same imaging, lab, or EKG across hospital and doctor bills | DB-2 | red |
| Balance above EOB patient responsibility; new bill after the insurer paid | DB-3 | red |
| Two claims for one visit (original plus corrected) | DB-4 | red |
| Paid at the desk and the insurer paid; credit balance not refunded | DB-5 | red |
| 99215/99205 for a short, simple visit; top DRG on a short stay | OB-1 | amber |
| 99285 or level-5 facility charge for a minor ER visit; 99291 without 30+ min | OB-2 | amber |
| Panel parts billed separately (lipid 80061, CMP 80053) | OB-3 | red |
| E/M-25 on the same day as a minor procedure; -59/XE/XS/XP/XU overrides | OB-4 | amber |
| Timed units above minutes (8-minute rule); units above the MUE | OB-5 | amber |
| Attending fee without GC or presence; incident-to without supervision | OB-6 | amber |
| Overnight "observation" G0378; inpatient rebilled as outpatient; no MOON | OB-7 | amber |
| Cost-share on preventive 99381-99397 or a screening lab | IN-1 | red |
| G0463, rev 051x "clinic/facility" charge at a doctor's-office-type visit | JF-1 | purple |
| Rev 068x trauma activation; short ER stay, sent home | JF-2 | purple |
| "Misc supplies," "sundry," rev 0270 with no detail | JF-3 | purple |
| Gloves, gauze, linens, or tissues billed outside the room charge | JF-4/5 | purple |
| Generic pills at many times retail (rev 025x/0637) | JF-6 | purple |
| Two "initial" IV codes; hydration under 31 min | JF-7 | amber |
| Statement, paper-bill, card-convenience, late, interest, admin, or chart fees | JF-8 to JF-11 | purple |
| Per-page fee for electronic records | JF-12 | purple |
| No-show, membership, or concierge fee | JF-13/14 | purple |
| 99421-99423 for a portal message | JF-15 | purple |
| Facility fee on a telehealth visit from home | JF-16 | purple |

## Double billing
- **DB-1 Duplicate code, same date.** Sort by date and code. If the insurer denied a line as a duplicate (CARC 18), the patient owes $0 on it. Example: one surgery billed as two (KFF, Aug 21, 2024: kffhealthnews.org/health-care-costs/bill-of-the-month-one-surgery-charged-for-two-collections-lawsuit/). Units per code per day are capped by MUEs: cms.gov/medicare/coding-billing/national-correct-coding-initiative-ncci-edits/medicare-ncci-medically-unlikely-edits-mues
- **DB-2 Facility plus professional overlap.** A global code already includes -26 (professional) and TC (technical), so global plus -26 is a double payment (CMS RAC topic 0116). Medicare's 3-day window bundles pre-admission tests into the inpatient claim: cms.gov/medicare/payment/prospective-payment-systems/acute-inpatient-pps/three-day-payment-window. A separate ER facility fee and ER doctor fee is normal.
- **DB-3 Rebilled after payment, or above the EOB.** Billed - adjustment - plan paid = patient responsibility. For Medicare, providers can't charge beyond the deductible and coinsurance (42 CFR 489.21: ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-G/part-489/subpart-B/section-489.21), and excess collections must be refunded (489.40). In-network contracts limit commercial bills the same way; the No Surprises Act covers emergency and out-of-network-at-in-network care: cms.gov/medical-bill-rights/help/dispute-a-bill
- **DB-4 Corrected claim plus original.** A replacement is bill type xx7 and a void is xx8, with the original claim number referenced. Otherwise it's a duplicate. Ask the biller to confirm the void.
- **DB-5 Billed to both insurer and patient.** A credit balance is owed back (Medicare 489.40-42). Nonprofit hospitals must refund overpayments after a financial-assistance approval (irs.gov/charities-non-profits/billing-and-collections-section-501r6). WA AG example, $410K refunds (Sep 29, 2026): atg.wa.gov

## Overbilling
- **OB-1 E/M upcoding.** The level is set by MDM or total time. Established patients: 99212 10-19 min, 99213 20-29, 99214 30-39, 99215 40-54. Ask for the note. Sources: cms.gov/files/document/mln006764-evaluation-management-services.pdf; OIG OEI-04-10-00180 (2012) on the drift to top levels; OIG OEI-02-18-00380 (2021) on top-severity DRGs. A high level can be legitimate.
- **OB-2 ER levels.** Professional levels are MDM-based. Facility levels follow the hospital's own criteria, which CMS requires to reflect resources (cms.gov/Regulations-and-Guidance/Guidance/Transmittals/downloads/r1139cp.pdf), so ask for the criteria. Critical care needs 30+ min. Triage alone can't be billed as an E/M.
- **OB-3 Unbundling.** NCCI procedure-to-procedure edits; when all parts of a panel are done, bill the panel. Sources: cms.gov/medicare/coding-billing/national-correct-coding-initiative-ncci-edits; 2026 manual at cms.gov/files/document/2026-ncci-medicare-policy-manual-all-chapters.pdf
- **OB-4 Modifier 25/59.** Modifier 25 is only for a significant, separately identifiable E/M. Modifier 59 and XE/XS/XP/XU are only for a distinct service, not merely a different code or diagnosis (cms.gov/files/document/mln1783722-proper-use-modifiers-59-xe-xp-xs-and-xu.pdf). OIG (2005) found 35% of modifier-25 claims and 40% of modifier-59 pairs noncompliant.
- **OB-5 Units and time.** 8-minute rule: 8-22 min = 1 unit, 23-37 = 2, 38-52 = 3 (cms.gov/Regulations-and-Guidance/Guidance/Manuals/Downloads/clm104c05.pdf). 99291 needs 30-74 min. Check the MUE.
- **OB-6 Supervision.** A teaching physician must be present for key portions and the claim uses GC (ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-B/part-415/subpart-D/section-415.172). Incident-to needs direct supervision; since 2026 that can be virtual (42 CFR 410.26).
- **OB-7 Observation vs inpatient.** Observation is outpatient: per-service coinsurance, self-administered drugs billed, no SNF 3-day credit. A MOON is required once observation passes 24h. The two-midnight rule applies. Alexander v. Azar appeals: cms.gov/medicare/appeals-grievances/original-medicare-appeals/hospital-appeals-change-inpatient-status-alexander-v-azar; medicare.gov/coverage/inpatient-hospital-care/inpatient-outpatient-status.
- **IN-1 Preventive care with cost-share.** The ACA requires $0 for USPSTF A/B services, ACIP vaccines, and HRSA services in-network (42 U.S.C. 300gg-13: law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/300gg-13; healthcare.gov/coverage/preventive-care-benefits/). Upheld in Kennedy v. Braidwood (Jun 27, 2025). A same-day -25 problem visit can carry cost-share. Fix the codes, then ask the insurer to reprocess.

## Junk fees (purple)
The FTC junk-fee rule (16 CFR 464, effective May 12, 2025) covers only tickets and lodging, not health care, but its ban on vague fee names is good dispute language: ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/rule-unfair-or-deceptive-fees-frequently-asked-questions. CFPB medical-debt guidance was withdrawn May 12, 2025, and the CFPB credit rule was vacated Jul 11, 2025. Cite the FDCPA and FCRA statutes instead.
- **JF-1 Facility fee** at an off-campus or hospital-based clinic (G0463, rev 051x, POS 19/22). See the state notes below. Example: $30 injections became $1,394 with a $1,262 facility fee (KFF, Mar 26, 2021). MD AG: UMMS paying $2.25M for undisclosed fees (oag.maryland.gov, Sep 25, 2026).
- **JF-2 Trauma activation (rev 068x).** Requires a designated trauma center, pre-hospital notification meeting field-triage criteria, and an actual team response. Medicare G0390 also needs 30+ min of critical care (CMS R1139CP). KFF: a $15,666 fee for a toddler was waived (Jul 2, 2018).
- **JF-3 Misc supplies.** Demand item-level detail (item, quantity, unit price, order). Payers bundle routine supplies.
- **JF-4 Routine supplies.** Inpatient room and board includes "minor medical and surgical supplies" (CMS PRM 15-1 §2202.6/§2203: cms.gov/files/document/r502pr1.pdf). Medicare cost rule; use it as the benchmark.
- **JF-5 Euphemisms ("mucus recovery system" = tissues).** PRM §2203.1 lists "paper tissues" as routine. The anecdote has no documented bill, so don't present it as a case.
- **JF-6 Pharmacy markup.** Hospital generics average about 11x retail (JACC 2023). Markups aren't illegal; argue reasonableness, the patient's own medications, and 501(r) AGB limits.
- **JF-7 IV push vs infusion.** Push is 15 min or less, infusion more than 15, hydration needs 31+ min. One initial code per encounter (CMS article A53778; NCCI Ch. 11).
- **JF-8 Statement fee.** Maine bars penalizing paper billing (10 M.R.S. §9420). Otherwise argue there was no agreement; for collectors, FDCPA §808(1) (law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/1692f).
- **JF-9 Card convenience fee.** CT, MA, and ME ban surcharges; CO caps them at 2%. Varies, so re-check (ncsl.org/financial-services/credit-or-debit-card-surcharges-statutes). Ask for a fee-free payment method.
- **JF-10 Late fees and interest.** CO caps medical-debt interest at 3% (SB23-093). AZ caps it at the lesser of 3% or the Treasury yield (Prop 209). NY consumer judgments carry 2% (CPLR 5004). Late fees pause during a No Surprises Act dispute. Bureaus don't report paid medical debt or debt under $500, and wait a year. MN bans medical-debt credit reporting (2024).
- **JF-11 Admin, chart, or claim-filing fees.** Medicare bars charging for filing claims (SSA §1848(g)(4)). OIG's 2004 alert covers extra charges for covered services: oig.hhs.gov/documents/other-guidance/911/FA033104AssignViolationI.pdf
- **JF-12 Records copy fees.** For the patient's own access, only cost-based labor, supplies, and postage; no per-page fee for electronic records; optional $6.50 flat fee (hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/2029/how-can-covered-entities-calculate-the-limited-fee/index.html). After Ciox v. Azar (2020), the limit doesn't apply to third-party directives.
- **JF-13 No-show fee.** Medicare allows it only if the same policy applies to all patients, and it can't be billed to Medicare (CMS MM5613). Many Medicaid programs ban it.
- **JF-14 Concierge or membership fee.** Can't cover Medicare-covered services (OIG alert, Mar 31, 2004; medicare.gov/coverage/concierge-care).
- **JF-15 Portal messages, 99421-99423.** Only for patient-initiated threads, 5+ min within 7 days, with consent. Usually not refills, scheduling, or brief follow-ups. KFF (Sep 14, 2023).
- **JF-16 Telehealth facility fee.** Medicare Q3014 isn't payable when the patient is at home (POS 10). States banning telehealth facility fees: CT, ME, MD, OH, WA (audio-only), NM (2026), MS. KFF (Apr 3, 2023).

## State facility-fee notes (US of Care tracker, Aug 2026: unitedstatesofcare.org; Georgetown CHIR). Re-verify before citing.
- **CT** §19a-508c: no facility fee for E/M or A/M at off-campus sites, and since 7/1/2024 on campus too, except ED, observation, and listed service lines. Telehealth ban. Uninsured capped at the Medicare rate. Contracts in effect on 7/1/2024 are grandfathered.
- **CO** HB23-1215: no facility fee for preventive services; notice required; AG enforces.
- **IN** HEA 1004 (2023): large nonprofit systems can't bill off-campus on the UB-04. HB 1003 (2025) covers office settings, but its scope is disputed, so verify.
- **ME** LD 1795 (2023): no facility fee off campus. LD 2271 (2024): telehealth ban.
- **MD**: notice required since 7/1/2021; telehealth ban (2021).
- **MN**: notice and reporting only.
- **NY** (2022): no facility fee for preventive or non-covered services without notice.
- **OH**: telehealth ban (ORC 4743.09).
- **TX**: freestanding-ER drive-thru ban plus disclosure; no general clinic ban found.
- **WA**: notice (RCW 70.01.040); audio-only telehealth ban (RCW 48.43.735).
- **NM** (2026): preventive, vaccine, and telehealth bans.

## Levers (blue)
- **No Surprises Act self-pay dispute:** billed $400+ above the Good Faith Estimate, file within 120 days, $25 fee (45 CFR 149.620).
- **501(r) financial assistance:** 240-day application window; collections pause; refunds after approval.
- **Price transparency:** only 49.4% of hospitals are fully compliant (PatientRightsAdvocate.org, Sep 2026); compare against the hospital's posted prices.
- **State AG complaints work:** MD UMMS facility fees, MN uninsured discounts, WA charity care, NY CityMD (Feb 11, 2025).

skills.name: medical-bill-dispute-templates
skills.description: Use when drafting any message to a medical biller, collector, or insurer during a bill audit: itemized-bill request, per-finding dispute, financial assistance, prompt-pay offer, reprocess/appeal, collections hold, or follow-up.
skills.content:
---
name: medical-bill-dispute-templates
description: >-
  Use when drafting any message to a medical biller, collector, or insurer
  during a bill audit: itemized-bill request, per-finding dispute, financial
  assistance, prompt-pay offer, reprocess/appeal, collections hold, or
  follow-up.
---
# Biller and insurer message templates
Use these when drafting audit messages. Fill them from the audit JSON, show each one as a draft, and send only after the user approves. Cite the KB ID (medical-billing-knowledge-base) for each finding.

Rules for every template:
- Fill `{{placeholders}}` from the audit JSON. Never send a template with an unfilled placeholder.
- Show each filled message to the user as a draft. Send it only after they approve that specific message. A declined send is final.
- Include only the identifiers the biller needs (account number, date of service, claim number). Don't add a diagnosis, SSN, or date of birth unless the user approves it for that message.
- Every message asks the biller to CC `{{tracking_email}}` (the bot inbox with a `+{{provider_tag}}` tag) so replies are tracked.
- Cite the knowledge-base rule and source for every finding. Label estimates as estimates.

Common placeholders: `{{patient_name}}`, `{{account_number}}`, `{{provider_name}}`, `{{insurer_name}}`, `{{member_id}}` (insurer messages only), `{{claim_number}}`, `{{dos}}`, `{{statement_date}}`, `{{amount_due}}`, `{{tracking_email}}`, `{{today}}`, `{{response_days}}` (default 30).

## (a) First message: itemized bill request and CC
Subject: Itemized bill request: account {{account_number}}, dates of service {{dos_range}}

Hello {{provider_name}} billing office,

I'm reviewing the statement dated {{statement_date}} for account {{account_number}} (balance {{amount_due}}). Please send:
1. A complete itemized bill for {{dos_range}}, showing each line's date of service, CPT/HCPCS code and modifiers, revenue code, units, and charge.
2. A copy of the UB-04 and/or CMS-1500 claim(s) sent to my insurer, with claim numbers.
3. A record of all payments and adjustments on the account (patient and insurer).
4. Your financial assistance policy and application, if you have one.

While I review the bill, please put the account on hold from collections, late fees, and interest.

Please CC {{tracking_email}} on all correspondence about this account.

Thank you,
{{patient_name}}

## (b) Per-finding dispute
Subject: Billing dispute: account {{account_number}}, {{finding_title}} ({{dos}})

Hello {{provider_name}} billing office,

I'm disputing the charge below on account {{account_number}}.

Finding {{finding_id}}: {{finding_title}}
- Line(s): {{line_numbers}}, code {{code}}, date {{dos}}, charge {{charge}}
- What's wrong: {{issue}}
- Evidence: {{evidence}}
- Rule: {{rule_cite}}, {{rule_url}} ({{rule_date}})

What I'm asking for: {{requested_fix}} (for example: remove the duplicate line and send a corrected itemized bill; re-code to the documented level and re-submit to my insurer; or send the documentation that supports this charge).

Please hold this amount from collections, late fees, and interest while it's under review, and reply within {{response_days}} days. If you think the charge is correct, please send the records that support it.

Please CC {{tracking_email}} on your reply.

Thank you,
{{patient_name}}

## (c) Financial assistance / IRS 501(r) request
Subject: Financial assistance application: account {{account_number}}

Hello {{provider_name}} patient financial services,

I'd like to apply for financial assistance (charity care) for account {{account_number}} (dates of service {{dos_range}}). Please send your financial assistance policy (FAP), the plain-language summary, the application, and the amounts generally billed (AGB) percentage you use.

If {{provider_name}} is a nonprofit hospital, IRS rules (Section 501(r)(6)) require it to suspend extraordinary collection actions while a complete application is pending, and to refund any amount I've paid above what I owe if I'm approved. Please hold the account from collections until you make a decision. [Source: https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/billing-and-collections-section-501r6]
{{optional: I also ask that you apply {{state_charity_law}}.}}

Please CC {{tracking_email}} on all correspondence.

Thank you,
{{patient_name}}

## (d) Prompt-pay / lump-sum discount (only on the corrected balance)
Subject: Payment offer: account {{account_number}}

Hello {{provider_name}} billing office,

Thank you for correcting account {{account_number}}. The corrected balance is {{corrected_balance}}.

I can pay {{offer_amount}} ({{offer_percent}}% of the corrected balance) in one payment within {{pay_within_days}} days if you'll accept it as payment in full. If you can't, please tell me your prompt-pay or self-pay discount, or offer an interest-free payment plan of {{monthly_amount}} a month.

Please confirm in writing that the account will show a $0 balance after payment and won't be reported or sent to collections. I'd like to pay through a method with no convenience fee.

Please CC {{tracking_email}} on your reply.

Thank you,
{{patient_name}}

## (e) Insurer: reprocess or appeal
Subject: Request to reprocess claim {{claim_number}} (member {{member_id}})

Hello {{insurer_name}},

Please reprocess claim {{claim_number}} for date of service {{dos}} from {{provider_name}}.
- Issue: {{issue}}
- What the EOB shows: {{eob_detail}}
- What it should be: {{expected_result}}
- Rule: {{rule_cite}}, {{rule_url}} ({{rule_date}})

(Preventive-care example: "CPT {{code}} is an in-network preventive service, and the ACA requires $0 cost-sharing (42 U.S.C. 300gg-13). Please reprocess at $0 patient responsibility.")

If you can't reprocess it, please treat this letter as a formal internal appeal and tell me your decision deadline and how to request an external review. Please send me a copy of the claim as received and any policy you relied on.

Thank you,
{{patient_name}}
(Reply to: {{tracking_email}})

## (f) Hold from collections
Subject: Collections hold request: account {{account_number}} (disputed)

Hello {{provider_name}} billing office (or {{collection_agency_name}}),

The balance on account {{account_number}} is in dispute. I sent my dispute on {{dispute_sent_date}}{{optional: , and my financial assistance application is pending}}.

Please:
1. Put the account on hold, and don't send it, sell it, or report it to collections or credit bureaus while the dispute is open.
2. Stop late fees and interest during the review.
3. Confirm in writing that you've done this.
{{if a debt collector: As a debt collector, please also send validation of the debt, including an itemized statement of the amount claimed.}}

Please CC {{tracking_email}} on your reply.

Thank you,
